## Open findings

Raised by the documentation itself, in part 7 of each model chapter and of D6, the pricing
tool's chapter. Each has a compensating control and an owner, and each row is the chapter's
own, word for word.

### D4 Business Credit Score

From [D4.7](score/limitations.qmd).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | No out-of-time sample: origination is a single cross-section, so temporal stability is untested. | Train and test are random splits of one cohort; PSI between them ({{< var score.psi_score >}} on the score) measures sampling noise, not drift. | Monitoring plan (D4.8): score and feature PSI on each new cohort, with redevelopment triggers. | Model developer | open |
| 2 | The gate population is not the lending population. | Held-out AUC {{< var score.pop.everyone.auc >}} on all applicants (the gate, {{< var score.gate >}}); {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the booked only. | Report both on every run; track the booked-only AUC beside the gate; consider gating on the booked population at redevelopment. | Model developer | open |
| 3 | Features with no causal role in the generator are in the model (`industry`, `entity_type`, `trade_lines`). | Together they carry {{< var score.var_share_structural >}} of the logit's variance on the held-out applicants. | Present but inert: remove at the next redevelopment; removal is a simplification, not a risk fix. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | The score distribution is concentrated in one band. | {{< var score.band.D.n >}} of {{< var score.n_test >}} held-out applicants ({{< var score.band_d_share >}}) fall in band D, limiting discrimination inside it. | Downstream decisions use the PD, not the band alone; review band boundaries at redevelopment. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The weight of evidence of `leverage` is not monotonic, although the generator's effect of leverage is. | Read in bin order, WoE is not monotonic in {{< var score.woe_nonmonotonic >}}; `monotonic_trend` is left at optbinning's `"auto"` default. | Set `monotonic_trend` explicitly for each numeric feature at the next redevelopment and re-verify the gate; until then, discrimination is unaffected, since every performance figure is measured with these bins. | Model developer | open |
| 6 | The model under-predicts default risk in band B on the booked population. | Observed / predicted {{< var score.band_booked.B.ratio >}} on the held-out booked in band B, outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance, on {{< var score.band_booked.B.defaults >}} defaults (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}). | Recalibrate band B, or apply a calibration overlay to it, at the next review; until then, monitor booked band B's observed / predicted on each cohort against the floor. | Model developer | open |

From [D5.7](adjudication/limitations.qmd).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|

Lift on the booked, {{< var adj.pop.booked.lift >}}×, still clears its {{< var adj.gate_lift >}}× gate. | Report both populations on every run; track the booked-only AUC and lift beside the gates; at redevelopment, weigh gating on the booked population and placing the zones on the scorecard's PD instead. | Model developer | open |
| 2 | Two policy rules can never fire on this data: the leverage cap and the request-to-revenue cap. | Leverage cap {{< var adj.policy.leverage_cap >}} against a largest leverage of {{< var adj.max_leverage >}}; request-to-revenue cap {{< var adj.policy.req_to_rev_cap >}} against a largest ratio of {{< var adj.max_req_to_rev >}}; {{< var adj.rule.leverage.n_all >}} and {{< var adj.rule.large_request.n_all >}} hits over all {{< var adj.n_applicants >}} applicants. | Treat both as untested controls: restate each limit on this data's definition of its ratio, or remove it, at the next policy review; until then, monitor every rule's hit rate and flag any rule with no hits. | Credit policy owner | open |
| 3 | The Approve zone under-predicts default, on the held-out booked and on all held-out applicants. | Observed / predicted in the Approve zone {{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.ratio >}} on the held-out booked ({{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.defaults >}} defaults) and {{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.ratio >}} on all held-out applicants ({{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.defaults >}} defaults), outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}). | Calibrate the PD at the next retrain, then recalibrate the zones; until then, monitor the Approve zone's observed / predicted on each cohort against the floor, and never read the PD as a default rate. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | The PD-zone cutoffs are set as quantiles over all applicants, held-out rows included. | `t_low` {{< var adj.t_low >}} and `t_high` {{< var adj.t_high >}} from all {{< var adj.n_applicants >}} applicants; from the training rows' in-sample PDs alone, {{< var adj.trainonly.t_low >}} and {{< var adj.trainonly.t_high >}}, which change {{< var adj.trainonly.changed >}} of {{< var adj.n_test >}} held-out decisions. | Take the cutoffs from training rows only, preferably from out-of-sample PDs, at the next retrain. Immaterial in effect today: no interim action beyond this record. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The lift gate's function is named `top_ventile_lift` but measures the top {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}}. | Measured on the function, its top group is {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}} of the rows, not a twentieth; the module docstring, the validation report, the metadata key and `verify.py` all call it `top-20%` lift. | Rename the function at the next change to `train.py`. The number is right and the gate is unaffected; until then, this record is the control. | Model developer | open |
| 6 | On held-out booked loans, the Decline zone over-predicts default. | Observed / predicted {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.ratio >}} in the Decline zone on the held-out booked, on {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.defaults >}} defaults among {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.n >}} files, outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}); inside it on all held-out applicants ({{< var adj.zone.everyone.Decline.ratio >}}). | Monitor and explain, do not recalibrate: track the booked Decline zone's observed / predicted on each cohort against the floor, and read it as a selection effect unless the all-applicant ratio moves too. | Model developer | open |

### D6 Pricing

From [D6.7](pricing/limitations.qmd). Pricing is a tool, not a model (D0); its findings are
about what its output means, what is untested and who governs its inputs.

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | The headline mispricing share measures the data generator's quotes, not a pricing practice. | The generator quotes each loan at break-even on its true PD plus `base_margin` ({{< var market.base_margin >}}), with no capital charge; clearing the hurdle needs the capital charge, {{< var pricing.capital_charge >}}, which exceeds the margin by {{< var pricing.capital_charge_less_margin >}}. A loan clears only where the scorecard's PD sits far enough below the quote's, or the quote's noise covers the gap: {{< var pricing.share_mispriced >}} of the {{< var pricing.n >}} booked loans do not. | Report the mispriced share as a demonstration of the measure on generated quotes, never as a finding about a book, wherever it is shown; before any use on real loans, measure against the bank's actual quoted rates. | Pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 2 | The tool's summary does not separate loans that lose money from loans that only miss the hurdle. | {{< var pricing.below_break_even.n >}} booked loans ({{< var pricing.below_break_even.share >}}), with \${{< var pricing.below_break_even.ead >}} of EAD, are quoted below break-even and have negative ROE; `portfolio_summary` returns one mispriced flag, its share and mispriced EAD, with no break-even measure, so they are counted among the {{< var pricing.n_mispriced >}} mispriced loans and not shown as such. | Report the below-break-even count and EAD beside the mispriced share (the facts recompute both on every `verify.py` run) and monitor them; add both to `portfolio_summary` at the next change to `pricing/`. | Pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 3 | In bands AAA to B, the hurdle-clearing and recommended rates rest on a PD that under-predicts default on the booked. | On the held-out booked the scorecard's observed / predicted is {{< var score.band_booked.B.ratio >}} in band B (D4 finding 6) and {{< var score.band_booked.A.ratio >}} and {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.ratio >}} in bands A and AAA (below the floor of {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults); a PD that is too low makes both rates too low. These bands also show the highest mispriced share; read from the generator's code, that concentration comes from finding 1's construction, not from the PD: mispriced share {{< var pricing.band.AAA.mispriced_rate >}} in band AAA and {{< var pricing.band.A.mispriced_rate >}} in band A, against {{< var pricing.best_band_rate >}} in band {{< var pricing.best_band >}}. | Re-run pricing after D4's band-B recalibration; until then, monitor the mispriced share and EAD by band beside D4's band calibration on the booked, and do not set a band's price floor from the recommended rates in bands AAA to B. | Pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named), with the model developer (D4) | open |
| 4 | `fee_rate` can be moved in the workbench but no test sets it, and the book-level functions have no unit tests. | `fee_rate` defaults to {{< var pricing.fee_rate >}} outside `MARKET`; none of the {{< var pricing.n_engine_tests >}} engine tests sets it, yet the v2 what-if accepts it and shows a slider for it. `price_population` and `portfolio_summary` are exercised only through the portal tests, the facts tests and `verify.py`'s comparison with the committed summary. | Add an engine test at a non-zero fee and unit tests of `price_population` and `portfolio_summary` at the next change to `pricing/`; until then, the facts re-check both rate identities at a fee of {{< var pricing.fee_probe >}} on every booked loan on every `verify.py` run ({{< var pricing.identity.fee >}}), which catches the waterfall and the rate solvers disagreeing about the fee, not a fee mishandled the same way in both. The book-level functions have no interim control beyond `verify.py`'s summary comparison. | Pricing tool developer | open |
| 5 | The market assumptions have no owner or change control beyond code review, and the cost of funds alone moves the outcome most. | `MARKET` is a dict in `shared/config.py` with no owner, effective date or change log. A {{< var pricing.sens.step >}} move in `cost_of_funds` takes the share clearing from {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} to {{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.up.share_clears >}} or {{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.down.share_clears >}}, the widest swing of the six assumptions; the same dict sets the generator's quotes and line increase's gate. | Name an owner for each assumption (6.4), keep a dated change log, and re-run 6.5, 6.6 and D8's gate before a change is used; until then, `verify.py` fails on any change to `MARKET` until the facts are rebuilt, and every change is reviewed and recorded as code (D9). | Pricing tool owner, with Treasury and Finance (all proposed; to be named) | open |

### D7 Early Warning

From [D7.7](ews/limitations.qmd). The model's low AUC is not among them: it is
indistinguishable from a reference model given every observable column, and even the
generator's noise-free logit reaches only {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} AUC on the same
accounts, which is why the gate is on top-decile capture (D7.9).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | The tier cutoffs are quantiles of in-sample probabilities, so on accounts the model has not seen the High tier holds far fewer accounts than it was set for and captures little. | `t_high` and `t_med` are the {{< var ews.q_high >}} and {{< var ews.q_med >}} quantiles over all {{< var ews.n_book >}} booked accounts, {{< var ews.n_train >}} of them training rows (training AUC {{< var ews.train.auc >}}). The book is {{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} High by construction; the held-out accounts are {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.share >}} High ({{< var ews.tier_ho.High.n >}} accounts), and the High tier catches {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.recall >}} of held-out deteriorations. PSI between the two tier mixes {{< var ews.tier_ho.psi_vs_book >}}. | At the next retrain, set the cutoffs from out-of-sample probabilities (cross-validated predictions on the training rows) and confirm the mix on the held-out accounts; until then, plan review capacity from the held-out mix, never from the book's tier counts, and monitor the tier mix of each new cohort against the intended one. | Model developer | open |
| 2 | The whole-book capture and AUC, and the module's default watchlist, are in-sample and must never be quoted as performance. | Over the whole book, capture {{< var ews.whole.capture >}} and AUC {{< var ews.whole.auc >}}, against {{< var ews.capture >}} and {{< var ews.auc >}} held out; {{< var ews.n_train >}} of the {{< var ews.n_book >}} accounts are training rows. The module's default watchlist of {{< var ews.watchlist.n >}} holds {{< var ews.watchlist.n_train >}} training rows and {{< var ews.watchlist.n_holdout >}} held-out accounts; its deterioration rate, {{< var ews.watchlist.rate >}}, is the model remembering its training labels. The portal serves the top {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n >}} of the same ranking and the v1 page shows {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n >}}: all training rows ({{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n_train >}} and {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n_train >}}), with deterioration rates of {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.rate >}} and {{< var ews.watchlist.page.rate >}}. | Quote held-out figures only (the portal's summary does; the facts label every whole-book figure in-sample); at the next retrain, score the book's training accounts with out-of-fold probabilities, so that the watchlist and tier counts on the existing book are out-of-sample; until then, read the watchlist as a list to review, never as evidence of accuracy. | Model developer, with the portal owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 3 | The capture gate is met narrowly: about a quarter of bootstrap resamples fall below it. | {{< var ews.capture_events >}} of {{< var ews.n_events_holdout >}} held-out deteriorations in the top decile, where the gate needs {{< var ews.gate.capture_events_needed >}}: a margin of {{< var ews.gate.capture_events_margin >}} accounts. Bootstrap 95% interval {{< var ews.boot.capture.lo >}}–{{< var ews.boot.capture.hi >}} against the {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} gate; {{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}} of {{< var ews.boot.n >}} resamples below it, with the model held fixed. The level was re-specified before the first commit, with results in view (7.9). | Report the interval and the margin beside the gate on every run (the facts do); in monitoring, treat one cohort below the gate as a review and two consecutive as a redevelopment trigger; at redevelopment, estimate capture over repeated splits rather than one. The gate itself is not changed. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | On AUC, the model is not distinguishable from the scorecard's PD alone. | Held-out AUC {{< var ews.auc >}} against {{< var ews.pd_score.auc >}} for `pd_score` alone; paired difference {{< var ews.pd_score.diff >}}, 95% interval {{< var ews.pd_score.diff_lo >}} to {{< var ews.pd_score.diff_hi >}}, which contains zero. `pd_score` alone captures {{< var ews.pd_score.capture >}}, below the gate — one measurement, with no paired interval. | Report the benchmark on every run (the facts do); at redevelopment, compare capture and AUC against `pd_score` with paired intervals and refit without the score, before keeping the behavioural model; until then, make no claim that the model ranks better than the score alone. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The Low tier under-predicts deterioration on the held-out accounts. | Observed {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.observed >}} against a mean probability of {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.predicted >}}: observed / predicted {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.ratio >}} on {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.events >}} deteriorations, outside the {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}–{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}} tolerance (the monitoring floor is {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}). The Low tier holds {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.recall >}} of held-out deteriorations. | Calibrate the probability at the next retrain on rows the trees were not fitted on; until then, never read `prob` as a deterioration rate, and monitor observed / predicted by tier on each cohort against the floor. | Model developer | open |
| 6 | The `DELINQUENCY` trigger's configured clause can never fire on this data; the trigger is in effect a hard-coded "any days past due". | `dpd_max >=` {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.threshold >}} (`EWS_TRIGGERS["{{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.config_key >}}"]`) fires by itself on {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.n_alone >}} accounts: `dpd_max` peaks at {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.feature_max >}}. All {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.n >}} flags ({{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.share >}} of the book) come from `dpd_recent >` {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_recent.threshold >}}, a clause that appears in `shared/config.py` only in a comment: its threshold is written in `triggers.py`, is not a key, and no configuration can change it. The only unit test of the trigger exercises the dead clause. | At the next policy review, restate the severe-delinquency threshold on this data's scale or remove it, move the `dpd_recent` threshold into `EWS_TRIGGERS`, and add a unit test in which `dpd_recent` alone fires; until then, the facts count every clause's firings alone on each `verify.py` run, and monitoring flags any clause that fires on no account. | Monitoring policy owner (proposed; to be named), with the model developer | open |
| 7 | The triggers beat the base rate only modestly and together fire on most of the book. | Any trigger on {{< var ews.trigger.any.share >}} of the book; a flagged held-out account deteriorates at {{< var ews.trigger.any.precision >}} against a base rate of {{< var ews.base_rate >}}. Single-trigger lifts over the base rate run from {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.lift >}}× to {{< var ews.trigger.high_utilization.lift >}}×: all below {{< var ews.gate.lift_min >}}×, against {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.lift >}}× for the High tier; `DELINQUENCY` alone fires on {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.share >}} of the book. | At the next policy review, re-set each threshold against this book's distribution with a stated precision or lift target, from a threshold sweep (not yet run, 7.6); until then, present triggers as reasons attached to a tier, never as a standalone alert list, and monitor each trigger's fire rate and precision. | Monitoring policy owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 8 | The label is drawn over the same months as the features, so the model's lead time — its stated purpose — is unmeasured. | The generator draws `{{< var ews.target >}}` from the true PD, utilisation over the panel's last quarter, the rise in utilisation over the panel and leverage, with no later period; `util_recent`, `utilization_onbook` and `util_drift` measure the same quantities. ### D8 Line Increase

From [D8.7](line_increase/limitations.qmd). That the model ranks well is not among them: it
clears its AUC gate, beats every single input and gets {{< var ceiling.li.share_of_reach >}} of
the way to the data's ceiling (D8.5). Nor is the overlap between the offers and Early Warning's
flags, which on the evidence is mostly mechanical (D8.7, observations).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | {{< var li.cohort_gate.n_cannot_fail >}} of the {{< var li.gate.n_gates >}} training gates cannot fail — the aggregate ROE gate by construction, the PD and utilisation gates on this book — so no gate tests the quality of the offered cohort. | {{< var li.cohort_gate.n_cannot_fail >}} of {{< var li.gate.n_gates >}} gates. ROE: the aggregate is an equity-weighted mean of per-loan ROEs that each clear the hurdle (lowest {{< var li.cohort_gate.roe.min_offers >}}, hurdle {{< var li.gate.roe_hurdle >}}). PD: the ceiling, {{< var li.offer_max_pd >}}, is the book's median, below its mean {{< var li.book_pd >}}. Utilisation: an amount needs utilisation above `target_util` ({{< var li.config.target_util >}}), so every account with one is at {{< var li.cohort_gate.util.min_amount >}} or more, above the book mean {{< var li.book_util >}}. Every {{< var li.sens.step >}} scenario in 8.6 passes all four cohort gates. | Show beside each gate whether it can fail (the facts and the headline table do); at the next gate review, add cohort gates that can fail, measured on the held-out offers' outcomes against the floor; until then, read the cohort gates as checks that the rules ran, never as evidence that the offers are good. The gates are not relaxed. | Model developer, with the credit policy owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 2 | The offer threshold is set on in-sample probabilities, and the offered cohort and the candidates the portal serves are mostly the model's training rows. | The threshold is the {{< var li.config.offer_quantile >}} quantile over all {{< var li.n_book >}} booked accounts, {{< var li.n_train >}} of them training rows (training AUC {{< var li.train.auc >}}). {{< var li.offers.n_train >}} of the {{< var li.n_offered >}} offers ({{< var li.offers.train_share >}}) are training rows; their label rate is {{< var li.offers.rate >}}, against {{< var li.offers_ho.observed >}} on the held-out offers. The portal's top {{< var li.served.portal.n >}} hold {{< var li.served.portal.n_train >}} training rows at a label rate of {{< var li.served.portal.rate >}}; the v1 page's top {{< var li.served.page.n >}}, {{< var li.served.page.n_train >}} at {{< var li.served.page.rate >}}. On held-out accounts the threshold passes {{< var li.thr.share_holdout >}}, against {{< var li.thr.share_book >}} intended. | Quote the held-out offers' figures only (the facts label every whole-book figure in-sample); at the next retrain, set the threshold on out-of-fold probabilities and score the book's training rows out of fold, as D7 findings 1 and 2 propose; until then, read the candidates list as a list to review, never as evidence of accuracy. | Model developer, with the portal owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 3 | The lift gate does not distinguish the model from a sort on one column. | {{< var li.baseline.n_pass_lift >}} of the {{< var li.baseline.n_numeric >}} numeric inputs, sorted alone on the held-out accounts, reach the {{< var li.gate.lift_min >}}× lift gate (utilisation {{< var li.baseline.utilization.lift >}}×, revenue {{< var li.baseline.revenue.lift >}}×); none reaches the {{< var li.gate.auc_min >}} AUC gate (best {{< var li.baseline.best.auc >}}). The model beats the best with a paired interval of {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff_lo >}} to {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff_hi >}}. | Report the best single input beside both gates on every run (the facts do); at the next gate review, restate the lift gate relative to the best single input; until then, treat the AUC gate as the binding test of the model. The gate is not changed by this finding. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | `LINE_INCREASE["roe_hurdle"]` is never read: the hurdle that decides offers is `MARKET`'s. | No file in `line_increase/src` reads the key ({{< var li.config.n_unread >}} unread key: `{{< var li.config.unread >}}`); `incremental_roe` and the aggregate gate use `MARKET["roe_hurdle"]` through the market argument. The two are equal today ({{< var li.config.roe_hurdle >}} and {{< var li.gate.roe_hurdle >}}); a change to the module's own key would change nothing. `MARKET` has no owner (D6 finding 5). | Remove the key, or pass it to `incremental_roe` as the hurdle, with a test that a change to it moves the offers; until then, change the hurdle only in `MARKET`, and the facts list every unread key on each `verify.py` run. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The incremental exposure assumes the increase is drawn at today's utilisation, an assumption no data support, and it understates the limit committed. | The {{< var li.n_offered >}} offers commit \${{< var li.econ.amount_total >}} of new limit; the exposure reported is \${{< var li.econ.exposure_total >}}. Per loan the ROE does not depend on the drawdown ({{< var li.econ.ead_invariance >}}); the aggregate does, slightly: {{< var li.econ.full_draw.agg_roe >}} fully drawn against {{< var li.agg_roe >}}, with the same {{< var li.econ.full_draw.n_offered >}} offers. The generator never grants an increase, so no drawdown is observed. | Report the committed amount beside the assumed exposure (the facts do; the portal's segments show only the assumed exposure); size limits and capital on the committed amount, never on the assumed exposure; before any real use, measure drawdown on granted increases. | Model developer, with the portfolio owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
| 6 | The label is constructed by the generator for every account, not observed after an increase, so what the model predicts has no real-world definition yet. | The generator draws `{{< var li.target >}}` from the true PD, utilisation above a level, revenue and later deterioration, plus noise, for all {{< var li.n_book >}} booked accounts; nothing in the data records an offer, a take-up, a drawdown or a repayment. | Before any real use, define the label as an observed outcome of an increase over a stated window, and plan for selection: the outcome exists only for accounts given increases (a randomised hold-out of offers is one design); until then, make no claim about how offered accounts would perform. | Model developer, with the credit policy owner (proposed; to be named) | open |
